land.text: Egypt, the only region left of the United Arab Republic since Syria seceded in 1961, with the Sinai under Israeli occupation

predecessors.note: The same state under a new name: 'renamed the country the Arab Republic of Egypt in 1971' (Egypt page). The united-arab-republic dossier (me-10-k) dates the renaming to September 1971 from its own page; this dossier gives the year only.

capitals.name: Cairo
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Capital and largest city: Cairo'. Coordinates from the gazetteer's place list.

minus.text: Egypt in its present frontier with the whole Sinai Peninsula, the Sinai held by Israel since June 1967
the Halaib Triangle, 20,580 km2: under the 1902 administrative boundary Sudan's, 'considered part of Sudan's Red Sea State' until the 1990s (Halaib Triangle page)

correction.text: Egypt in its present frontier with the whole Sinai Peninsula, the Sinai held by Israel since June 1967, without the Halaib Triangle (Sudan's by the 1902 administrative boundary)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1971-1972, before Cliopatria's row: the United Arab Republic row (1969-1972) overlaps these years and its dossier ends the UAR in September 1971, when Egypt 'renamed the country the Arab Republic of Egypt in 1971' (Egypt page). The shape is this row's 1973 shape (Egypt with the Sinai, which Israel occupied and the ledger hatches) minus the Halaib Triangle: the Triangle 'was considered part of Sudan's Red Sea State' and 'participated in all Sudanese elections until the last Sudanese election in the late 1980s' (Halaib Triangle page), and republic-of-sudan draws it for Sudan until 1999.

1,011,241 km2 for 1973-1975 in Cliopatria against the infobox's 1,010,408 km2 (ratio 1.00; the body gives 1,001,450 km2; no year on either). Corrected by cutting the Halaib Triangle (86 gazetteer cells, about 21,700 km2 for the page's 20,580 km2), which Cliopatria draws inside Egypt for all of 1973-2023 although Sudan administered it until the 1990s (Halaib Triangle page: 'joint control of the area remained in effect until 1992'; 'In January 2000, Sudan withdrew its forces'); the shape is then about 989,500 km2, ratio 0.98 to an infobox figure that includes the Triangle. The shape includes the whole Sinai (47,798 km2 in the gazetteer's Sinai region), which Israel held except the strip Egypt won in October 1973 ('seizing most of the east bank of the Suez Canal', Sinai page), plus one 253 km2 cell of the Gaza Strip at the Israeli border and about 5,000 km2 of edge cells along the 22nd parallel that reach into Sudan. The Sinai stays Egypt's under the occupation hatch.

keyframe_review.note: 950,107 km2 for 1976-1982: this Cliopatria shape drops the whole Sinai (0 of its cells in the gazetteer's Sinai region; Cliopatria's Israel shape for 1976-1982, 89,646 km2, holds it). Israel's presence was an occupation, ended by the peace-treaty withdrawal that 'ended in 1982' (Sinai page), so the Sinai stays Egypt's land under the hatch of the occupation events, as in the predecessor dossier (united-arab-republic, me-10-k). Corrected to the 1973 shape. Also without the Halaib Triangle, Sudan's until the 1990s (see the 1973 keyframe).

Effective 1983-1999 (the next keyframe takes over in 2000). Cliopatria's 1,011,241 km2 for 1983-2023 is the same outline as 1973 (ratio 1.00 to the infobox) and keeps the Halaib Triangle in Egypt throughout; cut here for 1983-1999, when 'joint control of the area remained in effect until 1992' and Egypt moved in only in 1994, Sudan withdrawing in January 2000 (Halaib Triangle page; ledger 1994-2000). Cliopatria restores the Sinai in 1983, a year late: 'completely turning over control of the Sinai to Egypt in 1982' (Egypt page); with the 1976 correction above the Sinai is already in the shape, so only the hatch ends (ledger, 1982). Taba stayed Israeli until 1989 (ledger).

Egypt with the Halaib Triangle, administered by Egypt alone since Sudan's withdrawal in January 2000; Cliopatria's 1983 shape unchanged

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 2000-2023, inside the span of Cliopatria's 1983 shape: 'In January 2000, Sudan withdrew its forces from the area, effectively ceding control of the border zone to Egypt' (Halaib Triangle page; ledger, January 2000). The shape is Cliopatria's own (1,011,241 km2) with the Triangle in; Sudan keeps the claim and Egypt 'has been refusing arbitration to date', so the land is Egypt's by administration, not by agreement. Bir Tawil, south of the 22nd parallel, is not in it.

1,011,241 km2, the 1983 outline repeated for 2024 (ratio 1.00 to the infobox). The Halaib Triangle (in the shape since the 2000 keyframe) has been administered by Egypt since Sudan withdrew in January 2000 although 'Egypt has been refusing arbitration to date' (Halaib page); Bir Tawil, south of the 22nd parallel, is 'a terra nullius, claimed by neither country' and is not in the shape.

the Halaib Triangle, 20,580 km2: under the 1902 administrative boundary Sudan's, 'considered part of Sudan's Red Sea State' until the 1990s (Halaib Triangle page)

region.text: Egypt with the Sinai, without the Halaib Triangle, Cairo its capital

ledger.note: 1971: Egypt takes the name Arab Republic of Egypt. The page: 'renamed the country the Arab Republic of Egypt in 1971', after Sadat 'assumed the presidency' on Nasser's death in 1970. It is the same state as the United Arab Republic's Egypt; the page gives the year, not the month. The Halaib Triangle is not in the shape until January 2000 (ledger, keyframes).

Carried over from the predecessor dossier: Israel has held the Sinai since the Six-Day War of June 1967 ('Israel occupied the entire Sinai Peninsula, and Gaza Strip from Egypt'). The year 1971 is this dossier's start, not the page's date.

region.text: both banks of the Suez Canal, where the Egyptian crossing and the Israeli crossing of 15-16 October were fought

ledger.note: 6 October 1973: Egypt crosses the Suez Canal. 'The war started on 6 October 1973, when the Arab coalition launched a surprise attack'; 'the Egyptian assault force of 32,000 infantry began crossing the canal in twelve waves'. The Egyptian front lies on both banks of the canal.

region.text: the east bank of the Suez Canal, 1,200 km2 held by Egypt at the ceasefire

ledger.note: 6 October 1973: Israel's hold on the east bank of the canal ends. 'On 6 October 1973, Egypt launched the Yom Kippur War, seizing most of the east bank of the Suez Canal while Israel seized even more area to its west' (Sinai page); at the final ceasefire 'Egyptian forces held 1,200 km2 on the eastern bank of the canal' (Yom Kippur War page). Typed occupation_end, not gain: the east bank lies inside the Sinai, which this dossier already counts as Egypt's land under the 1967 occupation hatch, and state-of-israel carries no loss for it (its ledger has only the occupation of the Sinai, 1967 to 1982).

region.text: both banks of the Suez Canal

ledger.note: 25 October 1973: the war ends. 'A second ceasefire on 25 October officially ended the conflict'; the first, of 22 October, had collapsed. The lines were not yet separated: the disengagement of 1974 follows.

region.text: the west bank of the Suez Canal, the ground Israel seized in 1973 (1,600 km2 at the ceasefire), outside the Sinai

ledger.note: 25 October 1973: Israel holds the west bank. 'On the night of 15 October, 750 of Colonel Matt's paratroopers crossed the canal in rubber dinghies'; at the final ceasefire 'Israeli forces held 1,600 km2 on the western bank of the canal.' The occupation is the reading of those forces holding Egyptian ground west of the canal. The hatch covers the west bank only (the canal band less the Sinai); the east bank is inside the Sinai hatch already.

region.text: the west bank of the Suez Canal seized in 1973, outside the Sinai

ledger.note: 1974: Israel gives up the ground it took in 1973. The Sinai page: 'Israel exchanged the ten kilometers along the east bank and territory seized in 1973 for a 1974 ceasefire.' The direction of the exchange on the east bank is not clear from the sentence; the west-bank ground seized in 1973 is the land Israel left. Neither the month nor the agreement's name is on the pages. The hatch ends on the west-bank pocket only; the east-bank ground Israel kept ends with the 1975 pull-back (next event).

1975: Israel pulls back from the canal and it reopens. The Sinai page: 'Israel withdrew from immediate proximity with the Suez Canal, with Egypt agreeing to permit passage of Israeli ships' and 'The canal was reopened in 1975'; the page does not date the Sinai Disengagement Agreements or name the ground handed over. Typed occupation_end, not gain: the ground is inside the Sinai, already Egypt's under the hatch, and state-of-israel has no loss for it.

region.text: all of the Sinai Peninsula except Taba

ledger.note: 1982: Israel completes its withdrawal from the Sinai. The Egypt page: 'completely turning over control of the Sinai to Egypt in 1982' (the 1979 peace treaty, signed 26 March 1979, in force January 1980: peace-treaty page); the Sinai page: Israel 'withdrew from all of the Sinai Peninsula except the contentious territory of Taba'. No day or month on the pages; the stages between 1979 and 1982 are not dated there. Pages opened again on the repair pass and silent on the stages and the day: Egypt-Israel peace treaty, Camp David Accords ('This process would take three years to complete', March 1979 to 1982), Taba, Egypt; the Sinai page says only that Israel 'withdrew in several stages, ending in 1982'.
1982: Israel keeps Taba. It 'withdrew from all of the Sinai Peninsula except the contentious territory of Taba', which stayed Israeli until the arbitration of 1989.

1989: Taba is returned to Egypt. Taba 'was returned after a ruling by a commission of arbitration in 1989'; the page gives no month. The Taba, Egypt page: 'By February 26, 1989, the negotiations were completed and the award was implemented' and 'Hosni Mubarak raised the Egyptian flag on the town on 19 March 1989'; the month is left open.

1994: Egypt moves into the Halaib Triangle. 'In 1994, the Egyptian military moved to take control of the area as a part of Red Sea Governorate.' Before that 'joint control of the area remained in effect until 1992, when Egypt objected to Sudan's granting of exploration rights'; after January 1995 Egypt 'strengthened its control of the Halaib Triangle, expelling Sudanese police and other officials'. The page gives the triangle as 20,580 km2, disputed between the 1899 line on the 22nd parallel and the 1902 administrative boundary.

January 2000: Sudan withdraws from the Halaib Triangle. 'In January 2000, Sudan withdrew its forces from the area, effectively ceding control of the border zone to Egypt.' Sudan has not renounced its claim ('Halayeb is Sudanese and will always be Sudanese', al-Bashir, 2010).

January 2000: Egypt administers the Halaib Triangle alone. Egypt's forces have administered it since Sudan's withdrawal, but 'Egypt has been refusing arbitration to date': control, not agreed sovereignty. Until then the Triangle is outside this dossier's shape (Sudan administered it, 'joint control of the area remained in effect until 1992'); the 2000 keyframe adds it, and republic-of-sudan's ledger has the mirror loss in January 2000.

region.text: the Red Sea islands of Tiran and Sanafir

ledger.note: 24 June 2017: Egypt cedes Tiran and Sanafir to Saudi Arabia. The Tiran Island page: 'The island's administration was transferred back to Saudi Arabia by Egypt in April 2016'; on 14 June 2017 Egypt's House Committee on Defence and National Security approved the transfer and parliament passed it; 'On Saturday 24 June 2017, President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi of Egypt ignored the court ruling and ratified the agreement' that cedes sovereignty over the two islands; Israel agreed on 14 July 2022. The islands are not in the gazetteer's land grid, so no keyframe changes; kingdom-of-saudi-arabia (another me-10 part) carries no mirror gain yet.

wars.name: Yom Kippur War

zones.text: both banks of the Suez Canal

wars.outcome: Egypt crossed the canal on 6 October 1973 and held 1,200 km2 of its east bank at the ceasefire of 25 October; Israel crossed on the night of 15 October and held 1,600 km2 of the west bank. A 1974 ceasefire returned the 1973 gains, the 1979 treaty the rest of the Sinai.
wars.note: The Sinai page puts the Egyptian seizure of 'most of the east bank' on 6 October 1973. The peace treaty of 26 March 1979 (in force January 1980) and the Camp David Accords of 1978 are in the Egypt and peace-treaty pages but moved no border until the 1982 withdrawal.

wars.name: Halaib Triangle dispute
wars.outcome: Egypt took control in 1994-1995 and Sudan withdrew its forces in January 2000; sovereignty remains disputed and Egypt refuses arbitration.
wars.note: Not a war in the strict sense: the page records an escalation over oil exploration rights in 1992, an Egyptian military move in 1994 and expulsions in 1995. The earlier crisis of February 1958 belongs to the united-arab-republic dossier.

certainty.note: Judgment, not read from a page: Egypt's frontiers with Libya, Sudan (the 22nd parallel) and Israel are treaty lines. The exceptions are the Sinai, where the front of 1973-1975 and the occupation to 1982 follow ceasefire lines, and the Halaib Triangle, where Sudan's 1902 administrative line and Egypt's 1899 line differ.
Taba was the last disputed point on the Israeli line until 1989. The Halaib Triangle stays disputed after 2000 ('Egypt has been refusing arbitration to date') and Bir Tawil is unclaimed.

notes: Written by me-10-l on 2026-10-25 from five pages (the budget). SHARED WIKIDATA Q79 with republic-of-egypt (Cliopatria 1953-1957): treated as a DIFFERENT dossier, as me-10-j and me-10-k did. Between them stands the United Arab Republic (1958-1971, its own dossier, whose successor is this one). It is one continuous state, so the colour agent may give the three the same hue; this dossier starts in 1971, the year the page gives for the renaming (the united-arab-republic dossier has September 1971 from its own page). Cliopatria leaves 1971-1972 uncovered by this row (its UAR row runs to 1972), hence the new 1971 keyframe. SINAI: Cliopatria's 1976-1982 shape drops the Sinai (Israel's shape holds it); this dossier keeps it in Egypt's shape under the occupation hatch, as the predecessor does, and carries the occupation_start from 1967 as an event at the start year. The pages date the 1973 and 1974 steps, the 1975 pull-back from the canal and the final withdrawal to the year 1982 only; the stages of 1979-1982 (the interim line, St Catherine, the oil fields) and the day of the final withdrawal are not on any page opened. GAZA: one cell of the Gaza Strip is inside every Cliopatria shape of the row (a cell at the Israeli border; Egypt's administration ended in June 1967), left unchanged. HALAIB (repaired 2026-10-25 after review): the shapes of 1971-1999 now exclude the Halaib Triangle (intersect of Natural Earth Egypt with a 120 km circle at 35.7E 22.6N, the spec republic-of-sudan uses, 86 cells), because Sudan administered it ('considered part of Sudan's Red Sea State', 'joint control ... until 1992') and republic-of-sudan draws it for Sudan until 1999; the 2000 keyframe adds it back, so the January 2000 gain changes the shape. The ledger events and the war zone use the same resolving spec; 'Halaib Triangle' is still not in the gazetteer's region list. NOT ON THE PAGES OPENED (page silent): the Egyptian-Libyan border war of 1977, the Sinai insurgency of 2011 on, the Philadelphi Corridor beyond the peace-treaty page's single sentence. NAMES FOR THE GAZETTEER: Halaib Triangle (region), Taba (place). REPAIR PASS 2026-10-25: (1) Halaib as above; verdicts of 1973 and 1983 are now adjust. (2) Ledger 1973-10 and 1975 are occupation_end, not gain: the canal ground is inside the Sinai hatch; state-of-israel has no matching end (its ledger ends the occupation only in 1982), so the mirror belongs to its author. Because the Sinai start is one event and the ends are three, the validator warns that two occupation_end events (1975, 1982) have no earlier start of their own; the hatch is the union of starts less the ends. (3) The 1974 end and the 1973 west-bank start are the west-bank pocket only (canal band less Sinai). (4) Tiran and Sanafir: loss to kingdom-of-saudi-arabia on 24 June 2017 (Tiran Island page), sub-grid so no keyframe; Saudi dossier needs the mirror gain. (5) Withdrawal stages 1979-1982 and the day of the final handover: not on the peace-treaty, Camp David, Taba or Sinai pages; left as a gap. NAMES FOR THE GAZETTEER (added): Tiran Island, Sanafir Island (places).
